about.title: Small lots in the village, **acreage outside it.**
body: The village of Ortonville sits on Kearsley Creek and calls itself the downtown of Brandon Township. Around it, the township is rolling hills, woodlands, wetlands and lakes, and that is what most yards out here look like.

Lot sizes run the whole range, from small village lots to acreage and parcels of ten acres or more. A village lot needs a careful mow and a clean edge; five acres needs a wide deck, a plan for the leaves and a long plowed drive.
We work in Ortonville and across Brandon Township from our shop on Embury Road in Grand Blanc.

points.title: Keep clippings out of Kearsley Creek
points.body: Kearsley Creek is a cold water trout stream that starts in Brandon Township, and the township's master plan names sediment from eroding banks, bare ground and roadside ditches as its main problem. So clippings, leaves and loose soil belong on the lawn, not in the ditch.

points.title: Dry sand uphill, wet muck below
points.body: Much of the village sits on sandy ground that drains fast, with heavier soil across much of the township and wet muck in its low spots. One lot can go from dry to soggy as it runs downhill.

points.title: Burning by permit
points.body: In Brandon Township, open burning takes a yearly permit from the Brandon Fire Department. Dry leaves are allowed and wet ones are not, and lots under 3 acres follow the burn calendar.

points.title: Gravel and back roads
points.body: The Road Commission for Oakland County runs every road in the township except M-15, and its gravel roads get sand rather than salt, since salt does little on gravel. A gravel drive gets plowed to move snow, not stone.

logistics.title: Getting an Ortonville job set up.
body: Out here the job is often about distance: long frontage to trim, a long drive to plow and a lot of ground between the house and the road. Rob walks it with you first, so the estimate fits the property instead of a guess.

Call or text Rob at [(810) 990-3040](tel:+18109903040), or use the [estimate form](/get-an-estimate/). Tell him whether you are in the village or the township, and whether the drive is paved or gravel.

faq.q: Do you work in Ortonville, MI?
faq.a: Yes. Grand Scapes works in Ortonville and Brandon Township: [weekly mowing](/lawn-mowing-ortonville-mi/), [landscaping](/landscaping-ortonville-mi/), [leaf removal](/leaf-removal-ortonville-mi/) and [snow removal](/snow-removal-ortonville-mi/), plus [spring cleanups](/spring-cleanup/), [mulch](/mulch-and-flower-beds/) and [shrub trimming](/shrub-trimming/). It starts with a free estimate.

faq.q: Is Ortonville part of Brandon Township?
faq.a: Yes. The Village of Ortonville sits inside Brandon Township and has its own council and DPW, while the Brandon Fire Department, with a station in the village, issues the burn permits. When you call, tell Rob which side of the village line you are on.

faq.q: Can I burn leaves in Ortonville?
faq.a: In Brandon Township, dry leaves can be burned with a yearly permit from the Brandon Fire Department, on calendar days for lots under 3 acres, and never within 50 feet of a building or in the road right of way. Inside the village, check with the village office first. Or have us haul them away in a [leaf cleanup](/leaf-removal-ortonville-mi/).

faq.q: Do you plow long driveways in Brandon Township?
faq.a: Yes. Before the season, Rob looks at the grade, the turns and where the snow can go on a long drive, then explains the options. We plow with our own trucks and can clear and salt the walks too.
